description.value: Cognitive emotion regulation condition requiring participants to down-regulate emotions elicited by negative pictures through cognitive self-distancing: adopting a detached third-person perspective and reminding themselves that the images were not real or related to them or their loved ones.

spans.text: In the CER condition of the regulation task, participants actively down-regulated emotions elicited by the negative pictures by means of cognitive self-distancing

spans.text: Participants indicated whether a negative picture or no picture would follow the CS via a button press

instructions.value: Participants predicted whether a negative picture or no picture would follow each conditioned stimulus by button press. During CER trials they used cognitive self-distancing, taking a detached third-person stance; during NoCER trials they attentively observed and let the images passively sink in without changing the evoked emotions.

spans.text: For the learning task, participants were asked to predict the occurrence of a US after a particular CS.

stimuli.value: Blue square or yellow pentagon conditioned stimuli, followed probabilistically by negative pictures from the International Affective Picture System or no picture; regulation instructions ('Distance' or 'Attend), fixation cross, and emotional-state rating scale from -3 to 3.

spans.text: The US (6 s) was a negative picture from the International Affective Picture System ( Lang et al., 1997 ), shown on 50% of the trials (Paired trials).
